messages:
sam-support: FYI Acme Prod (t-acme-01) reporting a sudden flood of 429s and p99 token latency spikes on dedicated pool reserved-east-3 since 09:12 UTC. Customer says they changed plan yesterday. snippet from client: `HTTP/1.1 429` body: \"quota exceeded\". Can someone take a look?
anya-reliability: on it — can you paste the tenant id + a sample request-id and any recent plan changes? also which pool is their dedicated?
sam-support: tenant t-acme-01, req id r_0xabc123, pool reserved-east-3. Plan change was from \"growth-100k\" -> \"enterprise-500k\" at 03:02 UTC yesterday. No other infra changes.
chris-eng: I pulled their quota record from rate-service: looks odd. quota config shows:
```json
{
  \"tenant\": \"t-acme-01\",
  \"units\": 500000,
  \"window\": 60,
  \"window_unit\": \"MINUTES\",
  \"pool_ceiling\": 500000
}
```
But the runtime expects window_unit either \"HOURS\" or \"MINUTES\" depending on rate_unit flag; migration script left rate_unit=MIN in metadata. If service reads the legacy flag, it divides differently.
devon-ops: autoscaler logs for reserved-east-3 around the time show no scale-up events — pool occupancy sat at ~82% and we hit 429s for acme specifically. looks like per-tenant admission was failing before we could trigger burst capacity.
sam-support: customer reported 429s for ~45 minutes before opening ticket, they started backing off.
chris-eng: reproduction quick test: run this loop from a workstation to simulate their traffic:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do \\
  curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\
       -d '{\"input\":\"test\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/reserved-east-3/generate || break; \\
done
```
You should see 429 around ~120 calls if window mismatched. On t-acme-01 I confirmed rate-service reported remaining=0 though overall pool had free capacity.
anya-reliability: that screams per-tenant units conversion bug. chris, can you show the migration diffs?
chris-eng: migration diff shows we migrated plans by writing units=500000 and window=60 with window_unit=\"MINUTES\" but the rate-service worker reading legacy flag used rate_multiplier=60 (treating it as hours). so effectively tenant got 60x fewer tokens than intended. I pushed a quick query to list all tenants with window_unit=\"MINUTES\" and rate_flag=LEGACY_MIN:
```sql
select tenant, units, window, window_unit, rate_flag from tenant_quotas where rate_flag = 'LEGACY_MIN';
```
Result set has ~12 tenants, acme included.
autoscale-bot: [AUTOSCALE] reserved-east-3: scale-up suppressed due to per-tenant admission failures. No autoscale trigger emitted between 09:10-09:30 UTC.
billing-eng: we should treat this as a customer-impacting misbilling risk too. If the tenant was downgraded effectively, they might be owed credits.
devon-ops: immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily patch rate-service to ignore legacy flag for tenants with window_unit=\"MINUTES\" OR 2) roll back plan change in admin console to previous plan. I can push #1 as a hotfix with a small window.
anya-reliability: do #1 as hotfix (safer for other tenants). chris, can you craft the hotfix? sam, please coordinate comms with Acme (apologize + ask them to hold off on any plan toggles). billing-eng prepare credit estimate.
chris-eng: will open PR to normalize units on read: detect window_unit==\"MINUTES\" and legacy flag -> multiply units by 60 before admission. also adding a CI check to catch mismatched window/rate_flag combos. will push in the next 20m and roll to rate-service fleet.
sam-support: messaging drafted to Acme: \"we found a quota migration bug that temporarily reduced your effective rate by ~60x; we're applying a hotfix and will follow up with credits and a timeline.\" sending now.
devon-ops: hotfix deployed to canary, observed tenant admission restored, acme reported success at 09:46 UTC. will roll to prod in 10m.
anya-reliability: followups: 1) postmortem of migration script, 2) add alert when pool shows global free capacity but per-tenant remaining==0 for top-tenants, 3) run sweep to fix other affected tenants. assigning owners: chris -> migration fix + CI, devon -> sweep + rollout, billing-eng -> credits + customer comms.
chris-eng: created issue #INF-8347 and linked PR. CI check added.
sam-support: Acme is satisfied with hotfix and credits offer, monitoring for 24h. closing slack once sweep completes. :white_check_mark:
